cues.text: I wonder if you could spare a few minutes to do a survey on transport. It won’t take long.
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Lovely. The survey is on behalf of the local council. They’d like to know about what transport you use any suggestions for improvement. Can I start by asking you how you travelled to town today?
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Sure. I came on the bus.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: Great. Now can I get a few details about yourself?
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Great. Thanks. And can I have your address?
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Oh, right. I know that area. It’s Bradfield, isn’t it?
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Great. And could I ask what your job is? Are you a student?
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: I’ve actually just finished my training. I’m a hairdresser.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: Oh, right. And one more question in this section. What is the reason for you coming into town today?
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Actually it’s not for shopping today, which would be my normal reason, but to see the dentist.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: Now in this last section I’d like you to give us some ideas about the facilities and arrangements in the city for getting to and from work, er, any suggestions you have for improvements.
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Well, something I’ve thought about for some time is that when I do walk and I’m doing a later shift, I think the lighting should be better.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: And of course, I think it’s a real shame they’ve been cutting down on the number of footpaths. They should have more of those. Then people would walk more.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: And, I don’t think there are enough trains. That’s why I don’t use them – you have to wait so long.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: Thanks. And finally I’d like to ask your opinion on cycling. As you may know, there’s a drive in the city to get more people to cycle to work.
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: But we realise that there are things which the council, but also employers, might do to help encourage workers to cycle to work.
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER

cues.text: Yep. Well, I have thought about it and where I work there are no safe places to leave your bikes.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: And also, I’d have to cycle uphill and on a hot day I’d arrive at work pretty sweaty so I think I’d need a shower somewhere at work.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: And I suppose the last thing is that I wouldn’t be all that confident about cycling on such busy roads. I think I’d like to see you offering training for that, you know. I’d feel a lot better about starting if that was the case.
cues.speaker: LUISA

cues.text: Well, that’s very helpful. Thank you very much for your time.
cues.speaker: INTERVIEWER
